title: Two Hours on a Wet Saturday: What Volunteers Really Take Home
title_zh: 湿漉漉的周六，两小时：志愿者真正带回家的是什么
intro_zh: 本文约 539 词，围绕“做志愿者的收获”展开，从健康、技能、视角、社交与边界感等角度说明志愿服务的真实回报，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，句子难度中等，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: At nine o'clock on a wet Saturday morning, the small kitchen of a community centre is already busy. Six volunteers are packing hot meals into boxes. By eleven, forty of those boxes will sit on the doorsteps of older people who live alone. Nobody in the room is paid, and most of them give up only two hours a week — yet almost all of them say they get more back than they give.
paragraphs.zh: 一个湿漉漉的周六早上九点，社区中心的小厨房已经忙了起来。六名志愿者正把热饭菜装进餐盒。到十一点，其中四十个餐盒会出现在独居老人的家门口。屋里没有一个人是拿报酬的，而且大多数人每周只抽出两个小时——然而几乎所有人都说，他们得到的比付出的更多。

paragraphs.en: The first surprise is how ordinary the work is. Volunteers rarely save the world; they take a shift at a food bank, read aloud in a hospital ward, or repair bicycles for children in the neighbourhood. Researchers who study volunteering say these small, repeated tasks matter most, because they are exactly what a small organisation can plan around. A hero who appears once is less useful than a helper who comes back.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个意外发现是：这份工作其实很平常。志愿者很少在拯救世界；他们是在食物救助站值一个班，在病房里给人朗读，或者为社区里的孩子修自行车。研究志愿服务的学者说，正是这些细小而重复的任务最重要，因为它们恰恰是一个小机构能够安排和依靠的东西。出现一次的英雄，不如一个会再回来的帮手。

paragraphs.en: The second surprise is physical. A large study of Americans over fifty found that people who volunteered about a hundred hours a year reported better health than those who did not, and the effect was strongest among those who volunteered mainly to help others rather than to feel better themselves. Sitting at home and worrying, it seems, is harder on the body than standing up and doing something.
paragraphs.zh: 第二个意外发现与身体有关。一项针对五十岁以上美国人的大型研究发现，每年志愿服务约一百小时的人，自评健康状况好于不做志愿服务的人；而且这种效应在那些主要为帮助他人、而非为让自己感觉更好而做志愿的人身上最明显。看来，坐在家里发愁，比站起来做点事情更伤身体。

paragraphs.en: There are practical gains too. Ask Lin, a nineteen-year-old student who spends Sunday mornings teaching older people to use a smartphone. In three months she has learned to explain a password reset six different ways, to repeat herself without irritation, and to be reliable: she is expected at ten, and someone is waiting by the door. Employers notice this. Two hours a week for a year is a hundred hours of real practice in listening, planning and staying calm.
paragraphs.zh: 还有实实在在的收益。问问林吧，她是一名十九岁的学生，每周日上午教老人使用智能手机。三个月里，她学会了用六种不同方式解释如何重设密码，学会了不厌其烦地重复，也学会了做到可靠：大家十点等着她，有人已经在门口等候。雇主会注意到这一点。每周两小时，坚持一年，就是一百小时关于倾听、安排和保持冷静的真实练习。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the most lasting reward is perspective. Volunteers see parts of a city that most of us never visit — the back room of a food bank, the corridor of a nursing home, the flat where a disabled man has waited three weeks for a simple repair. That knowledge is not comfortable. But it quietly changes what a person notices, and what they are willing to complain about.
paragraphs.zh: 或许最持久的回报是视角。志愿者会看到一座城市里我们大多数人从不去的地方——食物救助站的后屋、养老院的走廊、一位残障人士为一次简单的维修等了三周的那间公寓。这样的认识并不令人舒服，但它会悄悄改变一个人注意到什么，以及他愿意为什么而抱怨。

paragraphs.en: Volunteering also answers a quieter problem. Loneliness among young adults has risen sharply in the past decade, and a shared task is one of the easiest ways to meet people without the pressure of a party. You talk about boxes and labels first. Friendship arrives later, sideways, and it tends to last.
paragraphs.zh: 志愿服务还回应了一个更安静的问题。过去十年里，年轻人的孤独感急剧上升，而共同完成一项任务，是在没有聚会那种压力的情况下认识他人最容易的方式之一。你们先聊餐盒和标签，友谊后来才到，是侧着身子进来的，而且往往更持久。

paragraphs.en: None of this means saying yes to everything. A burden that never ends drives people away: studies of charities find that unclear tasks and a lack of training are the main reasons volunteers stop. Good programmes ask how many hours you can commit to, not how many hours you have. Two hours, kept honestly, beats twenty hours that end in silence.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切并不意味着对什么都说“好”。一个永远卸不下的负担会把人赶走：对慈善机构的研究发现，任务不清、缺乏培训是志愿者退出的主要原因。好的项目问的是你能投入几个小时，而不是你有多少个小时。老老实实守住的两小时，胜过最后悄无声息的二十小时。

paragraphs.en: So the honest answer to 'what do you get?' is not a number. You get an awareness of how your own street works, a few skills you can name out loud, and the steady confidence that comes from being expected somewhere at ten o'clock. Start small: one task, one afternoon, one name on a list. The return is rarely loud. It is simply there, week after week.
paragraphs.zh: 所以，对“你能得到什么”这个问题的诚实回答并不是一个数字。你得到的是一种对自家这条街如何运转的意识，几个能大声说出来的技能，以及那种因为十点钟有人在某处等着你而产生的稳定信心。从小处开始：一个任务、一个下午、名单上的一个名字。回报很少喧哗，它只是安安静静地在那里，一周又一周。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why small charities often fail to keep their volunteers.
The practical and personal gains that volunteering brings to the volunteer.
How a community kitchen prepares hot meals for older people.
The rising cost of looking after people who live alone.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文从健康、技能、视角、社交关系和边界感等角度说明“做志愿者能收获什么”，第一段即点明“get more back than they give”，故答案为 B。A、C、D 都只是文中零散细节或未提及的内容。

questions.q: According to the study mentioned in paragraph 3, the health benefit was strongest among people who volunteered mainly to
options: work more than a hundred hours a year
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段明确指出效应“strongest among those who volunteered mainly to help others rather than to feel better themselves”，即为帮助他人而做志愿的人，故选 B。注意 C 与原文正好相反。

questions.q: What does the writer suggest by saying 'A hero who appears once is less useful than a helper who comes back'?
options: Volunteers should avoid tasks that look too difficult.
Organisations depend more on steady, repeated help than on one-time effort.
Heroes are not welcome in small community groups.
Volunteers should come back every single day.
questions.explain: 推断题。该句出现在第二段，前文说小机构能依靠的正是那些细小而重复的任务，因此作者强调“可靠、持续出现”比“一次性的壮举”更有价值，B 最贴切。D 过度推断，文中建议的是每周两小时这样的可持续投入。

questions.q: In paragraph 5, the word 'perspective' is closest in meaning to
options: a way of understanding things gained from experience
a detailed plan for the future
a strong feeling of pity for others
an official rule of a charity
questions.explain: 词义题。第五段说志愿者看到了城市中别人看不到的部分，这种认识“quietly changes what a person notices”，可见 perspective 指“由经历形成的看待事物的角度”，故选 A。B、C、D 均与该词在此处的含义无关。
